mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% triggers a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) fall by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a contraction in consumer spending that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when RSAFS falls by more than 0.5%, or the average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% and a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below -50,000 indicates a severe labor market deterioration, which triggers a negative equity market reaction due to reduced consumer spending and corporate hiring cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS < -50,000, or the joint effect is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic expansion (GDP growth > 2.0% annualized), a decline in housing starts below 1,100,000 units signals a cooling housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and HOUST decline), or the average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).
